title: Access review scripts and audit schema runbook
summary: Runbook for automated quarterly access certification, lightweight day-to-day access review scripts, and a canonical audit log schema with SIEM mapping notes. Focused on operationalizing evidence collection and review across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
purpose: Provide a single place for engineers and reviewers to run access reviews, collect signed justification evidence, and push structured audit events into the SIEM. Reduce manual steps during compliance audits and speed up offboarding/role-change remediation.
scope: Applies to IAM entitlements managed by Redwood: API keys, service principals, console roles, dedicated pool ACLs, and private-deployment RBAC scopes. Excludes application-level (customer) roles stored outside Redwood control plane.
overview: This doc contains: 1) a compact roles matrix CSV for reviewers, 2) two policy templates (temporary access and emergency access), 3) the canonical audit event schema we emit from the control plane, 4) mapping guidance for Splunk/Elastic/Chronicle, and 5) lightweight automation scripts and GitHub Actions schedules to run periodic certification and archive evidence.

policy_templates:
Template: Temporary Access Request (short-lived)
- Purpose: short-lived justification for task-based privileges
- Fields: requester, justification, scope (roles), expiration (ISO8601), approver, ticket_id
- Enforcement: create time-limited credential via provisioning API, auto-revoke at expiration

Template: Emergency Access (break-glass)
- Purpose: mitigate operational incident where normal flows cannot be used
- Fields: requester, incident_ref, justification, start_time, approver_post_factum, TTL (max 8 hours)
- Audit: require after-action review within 48 hours and signed attestation
audit_log_schema:
Canonical audit event (json lines):
- event_time: ISO8601 timestamp (e.g. 2024-11-02T15:24:03Z)
- event_id: uuid4
- service: control-plane | serving-runtime | optimizer | console
- environment: hosted | dedicated | private
- actor_id: user:<email> | service:<service-name>
- actor_roles: [comma-separated role names] (string)
- action: string (e.g. iam.grant, iam.revoke, model.request, config.update)
- target_type: user | role | api-key | pool | model
- target_id: opaque id or human name
- result: success | failure | denied
- decision_reason: human-readable short reason (optional)
- request_id: correlation id passed through the stack
- trace_id: distributed trace id if available
- client_ip: ipv4/ipv6 (if applicable)
- auth_method: oauth | api_key | sso | service_token
- policy_snapshot: short hash referencing effective policy bundle (string)
- evidence_refs: semicolon list of signed artifacts (s3://bucket/path or git+sha)
- ttl_seconds: numeric (how long event retained in hot store)
- schema_version: v1
siem_field_mapping:
Mapping guidance (examples):
- SIEM common fields: timestamp -> event_time, host -> service, user -> actor_id, src_ip -> client_ip, event_id -> event_id
- ECS-friendly: ecs.version = 1, event.action = action, event.kind = event_type (audit), event.outcome = result, trace.id = trace_id
- Splunk props: sourcetype=redwood:audit, extract JSON, use event_time as _time
- Elastic ingest pipeline: parse JSON, map actor_id.keyword, environment.keyword, action.keyword, add ingest_tag: redwood_audit, set index lifecycle policy to hot->warm->cold based on ttl_seconds
- Example SIEM alert rule: if action=="iam.revoke" and result=="failure" and environment=="private" then create high-sev ticket and notify sec-oncall
access_review_workflow:
Periodic certification flow (recommended):
1) GitHub Actions schedule: 0 9 * * 1 (first Monday 9am UTC of quarter) triggers workflows/access_certify.yaml
2) Script collects current entitlements, collapses by owner, and emits per-owner CSV to secure workspace (s3://redwood-compliance/reviews/quarterly/2024-Q3/)
3) Owners get email + Slack DM with a one-click link to Accept / Revoke / Request more info (link includes prefilled evidence upload form)
4) Requests for revocation open a ticket (Jira compliance-REV-####) and start revocation playbook. Evidence attachments auto-signed and hashed.
5) Compliance team runs sampling QA (5% of accepted items) and signs off in Confluence page.

Notes: owners are derived from the owner_tag on the role or the last approver in the role history. Escalation happens automatically after 7 days and CCs the manager and team lead.
evidence_automation_playbook:
Automation components:
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/compliance-evidence (scripts/, actions/, playbooks/)
- primary scripts: scripts/generate_entitlement_report.py, scripts/upload_evidence.py, scripts/verify_signatures.sh
- signing: all evidence PDFs are signed with our KMS key via a signing lambda; the signature is stored adjacent to the artifact and the signature hash is included in evidence_refs in audit events
- retention: signed artifacts archived to compliant S3 bucket with bucket lifecycle (10y archive, encrypted with CMK), hot copies kept 90 days for auditors
- verification: verification script cross-checks evidence_refs in events against S3 list, checks signature validity, and produces a verification_report.json (stored as stringified JSON in the audit event for the certification job)
environment_differences: Hosted: centralized audit pipeline, Redwood-managed keys, faster rotation windows, reviewers are team leads via self-serve console. Dedicated: audit events include pool_id and tenant_tag; evidence artifacts remain in Redwood-managed storage unless customer chooses export; privacy options: scrub PII before SIEM export. Private: control plane is customer-provided; we ship a signed audit-forwarder (container) that normalizes local events to canonical schema and forwards to customer SIEM endpoint; default retention is controlled by customer but we recommend same policies.
